title: The Water-Carrier and the Goldsmith's Wife (Español)

keywords: the water-carrier and the goldsmith's wife
full_text:
In a quiet quarter of Baghdad lived an honest water-carrier named Salih who had served the same wealthy goldsmith’s household for thirty years. Every morning and evening, Salih carried heavy goat-skins of fresh river water into the courtyard, filling the kitchen jars and garden basins.

Throughout those thirty years, Salih had conducted himself with such impeccable modesty, lowering his gaze and respecting the privacy of the home, that the goldsmith trusted him as a member of his own family, allowing him to enter without announcing his arrival.

One afternoon, as Salih poured water into the basin, the goldsmith’s wife stepped onto the veranda to adjust the jasmine trellis, her golden bracelet catching the light. In that fleeting second, a sudden impulse of thoughtless indiscretion seized Salih's mind; he reached out and touched the maiden's hand before recovering his senses and fleeing the courtyard in burning shame.

The wife stood stunned, deeply offended by the unexpected breach of trust. When her husband returned from the bazaar that evening, she noticed that he looked unusually somber.

The goldsmith embraced his wife and sighed: 'A strange and shameful thing befell me today in the bazaar. A noble lady came to my shop to purchase a golden ring. As I slid the ring upon her finger, a sudden thoughtless impulse overcame my discipline, and I squeezed her hand! I instantly repented, but my soul has been tormented by remorse all afternoon.'

His wife looked at him with wide, knowing eyes and replied: 'Now I understand! Today, after thirty years of flawless courtesy, our water-carrier touched my hand in the courtyard! Your thoughtless action in the bazaar was reflected back upon your own house.'

The goldsmith wept in realization that one’s conduct in public returns to one’s own hearth.

The next morning, the water-carrier arrived with ashes on his head, begging for forgiveness with sincere tears. The goldsmith embraced him, both having learned that integrity requires unceasing vigilance in every thought, word, and deed.
moral: A momentary lapse in discipline can tarnish thirty years of honor; constant vigilance preserves integrity. [ES]
